name: Memory-care and assisted-living communities
fit: Not every senior community belongs in a 'healing music' directory, but memory-care units, caregiver-family nights, hospice memorials and life-review programs are high-fit. Prioritize communities with dedicated memory care and activity/wellness directors. Ask for the Life Enrichment Director, Memory Care Director or Resident Engagement Director. Offer a small, conversation-friendly acoustic visit rather than a standard entertainment set.

name: Funeral homes not listed above
fit: Nearly every funeral home has aftercare relationships and annual remembrance needs. Ask specifically about aftercare, grief support, holiday memorials, candlelight services and anniversary remembrance events. The relevant person is often a funeral director, aftercare coordinator or community-relations director.

name: Disease-specific support groups
fit: Search for local ALS, MS, stroke, brain injury, ostomy, Parkinson’s, cancer-type, heart failure, transplant, chronic pain and rare-disease groups. Hospital social workers and national disease organizations can connect you to local volunteer leaders. A song may fit caregiver appreciation, awareness events or milestone gatherings even when it does not fit a normal support meeting.

name: University counseling and campus ministry
fit: College of Charleston, The Citadel, Charleston Southern University and Trident Technical College all have students navigating loss, parental illness, identity transitions, recovery and mental-health strain. Ask counseling outreach staff or campus ministry about remembrance events, wellness weeks and reflective gatherings rather than therapy sessions.

name: First-responder and public-safety wellness
fit: Police, fire, EMS, dispatch and coroner teams encounter traumatic loss repeatedly. Employee-assistance, peer-support and chaplain programs may host remembrance, wellness or critical-incident recovery events. Offer music only through the wellness/chaplain/peer-support lead.

name: Pet-loss communities
fit: Veterinary hospitals, emergency/specialty veterinary centers, animal shelters and private grief counselors sometimes hold pet memorials. Pet loss is often disenfranchised grief and can be a particularly receptive setting for a song about companionship and memory.

name: Divorce, infertility and identity-transition groups
fit: Therapists and faith communities run groups for divorce, infertility, empty nest, retirement, caregiving identity, job loss and major transitions. Search Psychology Today and church care pages. Your strongest angle is not 'grief music' but music about change, what cannot be recovered, and rebuilding identity.

name: Staff-care / caregiver appreciation
fit: Hospital nurses, hospice staff, social workers, chaplains, CNAs and professional caregivers experience secondary grief. Staff appreciation, Schwartz-round-style reflection, hospice memorials and caregiver retreats may be easier to enter than patient-facing settings and can still be deeply meaningful.
